summary: @omniwatch-wick/cli posts host identifiers to hardcoded Cloudflare Workers / Vercel endpoints
details: The package's bin/omniwatch.js imports child_process, os, http, and https, reads os.userInfo() and hostname, and issues POST requests to two hardcoded endpoints: https://agentpolice-api.vedantn06soni.workers.dev and https://night-watch-indol.vercel.app. Platform-branching on process.platform is present. The observed shape — collecting host/user identifiers and sending them to author-controlled cloud endpoints — is consistent with either a monitoring/telemetry agent (as the package name 'omniwatch' / 'night-watch' suggests) or installer-side reconnaissance. Because the file is a bin/CLI entry (not a package.json lifecycle hook and not a require-time side effect of a library main), the network activity fires when the operator explicitly runs the CLI, not on npm install. Whether the collected identifiers and any additional data sent to the author's Workers/Vercel endpoints exceed what a user knowingly opts into by running a 'watch'-style CLI is a trust/disclosure judgment that warrants human review of the maintainer and the endpoint behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
